# Video: 100,000 rows in a browser grid without blocking the page — a 60–90 s demo

## Context

The operator, Fri 2026-10-30 23:xx CET: Saturday is Showoff Saturday on r/webdev; the post (#20184) is about **the Neo.mjs grid** as a whole, and the video shows the same subject moving — the grid off the main thread, on Neo's own issues; 13.3's features are its newest beats, not the subject. The November operating page (private, business #19) commits to one or two YouTube videos a week from Mon Nov 2, each publish request naming its search term, title and cover before the operator's upload click, the publish recorded in the outbound ledger (business #21). The operator's own datum (Oct 30): the FM film that showed the roster and the activity view got 8 views; a 19-second short of the 3D engine with no narration got 1,100 views in two hours — a film shows the good stuff moving, or it shows nothing. *(Re-cut 23:4x CET with #20184: the grid, not the release.)*

## The Problem

The showcase is live and nothing moves on YouTube. The 13.2 Workstation film ([KESyjFmOz0k](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KESyjFmOz0k), 1:46, narrated, chaptered) is the craft precedent and reached 183 views in 13 days — the reach problem, not the craft; this one is short, visible in the first three seconds, and published through the gate.

## The Architectural Reality

- **The subject:** https://neomjs.com/examples/grid/issues/index.html — Neo's own 497 most recent issues; `contentSizedRows` (#19658), `columnMenu` value pickers with live counts (#19643), the `searchToolbar` (#19794), the fixed-height toggle, the light/dark switch (`examples/grid/issues/MainContainer.mjs`); and the Workstation's 100,000-row grid for the scale beat (13.3.1's notes name it).
- **Authority:** `.agents/skills/video-create/` — claims bound to evidence, app choreography, voice, native capture, composition, QA, publication and artifact lineage; its production record template lives in an owner-private, gitignored root. Native captures only, no mockups, no staged data.
- **The gate:** business #19's publish request (title, cover, search term) before the operator's click; the FM publish gate (ADR 0042, #19575) carries the fields for the socials.

## The Fix

Five beats, 60–90 s, 1080p, captions over narration (the short that worked had none; a peer's voice only if the skill's QA passes it):

1. **Scale** — the benchmark app's 100,000 rows × 200 columns (`neomjs/benchmarks`, `apps/bigData/neo`) taking the 50→200-column update with the main-thread probe on screen: long tasks 0 ms, the RAF needle at ~16.7 ms; one caption: the grid's logic runs in a worker, not on the main thread (the report: 7.2× faster than React + AG Grid Community on this update, which stalls 378 ms — Chromium, production). If the benchmark app is not capturable in time, the Workstation's 100,000-row grid scrolling and re-sorting.
2. **The choice** — the issues showcase with fixed rows clipping titles, then the toggle: every row the height of its text, the row under the cursor holding still.
3. **Filter by value** — the Area header menu, counts changing as the State filter is applied.
4. **Search** — one word across title and summary; *Clear filters* leaves the sort alone.
5. **Dark, and out** — the theme switch, the issue count, the URL as the last frame.

**The YouTube title names the viewer's problem and carries the search term — never the product name** (the operator, 23:5x CET: a product-name title creates zero traction); candidates (the operator killed the scale-number, the engineering-statement and the competitor-comparison forms as a stranger — see #20184 step 0): *What happens when a data grid lives in a web worker* · *The main thread is the wrong place for a data grid* · *A data grid that cannot touch the DOM — 100k rows, live*; the numbers go in the description and the first caption, never the title; the rule for title, thumbnail and the first three seconds: find the reasons the target viewer would not click and would not watch past three seconds, answered in the publish request, with a second reader's hostile pass before the operator's click; never "the fastest", which the report's own scrolling table (AG Grid 1.7–2.8× faster there, #20125 fixed after the run) would falsify in the first comment; the cover frame shows the grid moving, not a logo; the worst-parse test on the title (read it as a skeptical stranger with zero context — "without X" only before a cost, never before a capability; see #20184 step 0). Then the publish request on business #19 (title, cover frame, search term — area G names it; proposed *javascript data grid 100k rows*), the operator's upload, the `video` row in business #21's ledger, and the link in #20184's Showoff blurb.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] AC-1 The capture is native, from the live showcase and the Workstation at named commits; every on-screen claim is true against the release notes (the skill's evidence ledger in the production record).
- [ ] AC-2 ≤ 90 s; captions readable at 1080p; the first visible change inside three seconds.
- [ ] AC-3 The publish request (title, cover, term) is on business #19 before the operator's click.
- [ ] AC-4 (post-publish) The YouTube URL and the ledger row are on this ticket; #20184's blurb links it.

## Out of Scope

Stage shorts (their own route); a Workstation docking film (a film of its own); the Medium post (#20184).

## Avoided Traps

- A product-name title: accurate and invisible; the title is the problem, the term, the number.
- The roster-and-activity-view mistake: nothing in frame that does not move or change.
- A mockup or a staged dataset: the showcase is Neo's own issues, live.
- A features reel: the scale beat comes first because the worker is the thing a stranger has not seen.
- Uploading without the gate fields: titles and covers were the last season's failure.
